fieldMarks: Grizzled (peppery) gray upperparts; reddish-brown on neck sides, chest, belly and legs.
Tail about one-third of total length with a distinct black stripe along the top and a black tip.
behavior: The only North American canid that climbs trees, using hooked claws to escape predators or reach food.
Mainly nocturnal and solitary outside breeding and pup rearing.
Dens in hollow trees and logs, rock crevices and burrows.
Omnivorous: small mammals, insects, birds and fruit (apples, berries, wild grapes); caches surplus food.
habitat: Deciduous forest mixed with brushy woodland and rocky terrain, often near water and where woodland meets farmland.
range: From southern Canada through most of the continental US to Colombia and Venezuela, absent from much of the Great Plains and the mountainous Northwest.

lookalikes.name: Red fox
lookalikes.howToTell: Red foxes have black legs and a white-tipped tail; the gray fox's tail has a black stripe and black tip.
